title: Interactive QuickForge SDK Wizard — notebook (draft)
content:
Context and intent:
This is a working notebook for an interactive, in-console "QuickForge" onboarding wizard aimed at first-time SDK users. Goal: reduce time-to-first-success from sign-up -> working sample app to under 10 minutes. Focused on the common pain points we see in onboarding telemetry: API keys, environment setup, common network errors, and demo prompt tuning.

Audience:
- Software engineers evaluating Redwood API
- Platform/integrator engineers doing PoC
- Solutions engineers running live demos

High-level goals (measurable):
- First request success rate >= 85% for new signups in sandbox within 10 minutes
- Telemetry flagging common failure types (auth, network, schema mismatch) with first-class labels
- Provide an opt-in guided wizard that can be embedded in web sandbox, CLI, or interactive notebook

Constraints / non-goals:
- This is not a full replacement for the SDK quickstart README; it's a guided path that surfaces targeted fixes and live checks
- Avoid heavy-weight browser-only flows; must support CLI and headless environments

Core flow (interactive sequence):
1) Verify API key (automated): quick POST to /v1/auth/verify -> friendly error codes (401 -> hint: "check org vs user key")
2) Env check: node/python/cli detection, check for node >=16/python >=3.9; shell perms; proxy env vars
3) Telemetry opt-in box (explain data captured: token metrics, latencies, sample prompts, no PII unless user opts-in)
4) Run sample app scaffold (choice: chat, summarization, embedder) -> scaffold creates minimal folder with snippets and .env.example
5) Run smoke request with sample prompt (shows streaming output if available)
6) Failure triage helper (if smoke fails): interactive checklist with 3 quick fix buttons: rotate key, open network diagnostics, switch model to small-compat variant
7) Post-success next steps: instrumenting telemetry, adding rate limits & retries, selecting dedicated vs hosted for scale

Example quick CLI transcript (prototype UX):
> quickforge init
> detect runtime: node
> (prompt) Allow anonymous telemetry? (y/n) y
> running verify -> OK (org key)
> creating sample/chat-app -> created ./quickforge-chat
> attempt request -> stream: "Hello from Redwood!"
> DONE in 5.1s

Key implementation notes (engineering):
- Lightweight back-end check service lives in developer sandbox infra; it proxies only auth check and returns canonical error hints (mapping table maintained in GH).
- All wizard steps are deterministic and idempotent; scaffolds should be re-runnable (append -2 if folder exists).
- Provide a minimal browser-based component and a pure-CLI mode; share business logic as a small package (quickforge-core) consumed by both frontends.
- Telemetry events schema: event_type, step, ok/fail, duration_ms, error_code, example_token_count (optional). Keep schema stable and versioned.

Telemetry probes (what we capture):
- step_attempt (init, verify, scaffold, smoke)
- step_result (ok/fail)
- error_category (auth, net, quota, model-incompat)
- latency_ms
- sample_prompt_hash (to detect identical test prompts without storing PII)
Notes: must show opt-in consent UI and never send raw user-provided content unless they opt in explicitly.

Failure mode triage (common cases we've seen):
- 401 Unauthorized: often wrong key/tokens for org vs user. Suggest: "Did you paste the right key? try 'redwood keys list'" + link to common pr docs
- DNS / proxy: environment has corporate proxy -> detect HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY and show command to test via curl
- Streaming not working: firewall blocking websockets -> fallback to polled mode
- Model mismatch: long prompt + small model -> suggest sample smaller prompt or switch to model-8k-compat

User copy + microcopy drafts (for UI + CLI):
- "Welcome to QuickForge — we'll check your setup and create a tiny sample app. This will only take ~2 minutes."
- "We collect anonymous telemetry that helps us prioritize fixes. No prompt text is collected unless you opt in."
- Error hint: "401 — API key rejected. If you used a personal key, try creating an org key from Console > API Keys."

Rollout plan (phases):
- Alpha: internal-only, internal SDK beta testers + SEs (2 weeks) -> gather failure taxonomy
- Beta: limited customer sandbox + docs (4 weeks) -> enable analytics dashboard for teams
- GA: opt-in persisted UI in Playground, CLI installed by default in npm/pip packages (8–12 weeks)

Metrics to watch during rollout:
- first-request-success-rate
- time-to-first-success (median, p90)
- telemetry-opt-in-rate
- common error distribution (top 5)

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- UX: how intrusive should the telemetry consent be? (banner vs modal vs CLI prompt persisted?)
- infra: cost of proxy verify calls at scale — throttle? batch? cache results per key for 5 minutes?
- security: can we validate keys without proxying full requests (we should avoid storing keys on our side)
- docs: produce a single-page cheat sheet for SEs with 'If X -> do Y' mappings

Links and references:
- GH prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-wizard (PR #42 contains core mapping table)
- Slack: #devexp-onboarding thread (see messages on 2024-10-29)
- Jira: DX-128 (tracking alpha run)

Appendix: quick checklist for SEs when debugging a failed smoke run:
- confirm key visible in env (echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY)
- run curl against /v1/auth/verify and paste response in ticket
- check HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY and try with --no-proxy
- try smaller model (model-8k-compat)

Notes to self (fragments):
- consider adding guided prompt tuner post-success (show token cost, suggest shorter phrasing)
- maybe reuse onboarding copy from hosted-playground but keep CLI language terse
- scope MVP to chat + embedder only (summarize later)

End of notebook. This is intentionally conversational — capture ideas, link to prototype artifacts, and iterate with SEs on wording.
